title: Twenty-two edges, by hand
spec: M01 · nodes, then edges, then the tag that makes an edge trustworthy
intro: Build orderflow's graph one primitive at a time — nodes, edges, provenance — and finish on the question a file listing structurally cannot answer. Small enough that you can audit every claim by hand.
foot: Every number here comes from python labs/shared_tools/kg_extract.py labs/sample-project · build it yourself in labs/M01-graph-fundamentals/

steps.title: What the file listing refuses to tell you
narrative: Start where every agent starts: a directory. orderflow is fourteen importable Python modules across three services and a shared/ folder, and the listing tells you exactly one thing — where each file sits on disk.

It does not tell you that billing and notifications, siblings in the tree, are intimate at runtime: billing publishes the very events notifications consumes. Directories encode location. Only an edge can encode who talks to whom.
Grep is the usual next move, and it has its own blind spot. Search for one symbol and count what comes back.
steps.youDo: grep -rn decode_jwt labs/sample-project — then look at each hit and ask which of them is a call.

cells: prose that happens to be correct

steps.title: Nodes — name every thing worth pointing at
narrative: The first primitive is the easy one. Walk every .py file, and every construct with a name and a location becomes a node: one per importable module, one per def, one per class.

Thirty-six nodes fall out of fourteen modules. The count is boring; the shape of a node is not. Each one carries an id you can address it by, a kind, and the file and line it came from — so every later answer is traceable back to source.
steps.youDo: python labs/shared_tools/kg_extract.py labs/sample-project --out graph.json, then open graph.json and find function:shared.auth.decode_jwt.

steps.title: Edges — and the direction is the whole point
narrative: Nodes alone are still a listing with better labels. The edges are what make it a graph, and two properties do all the work.

Directed: verify_token → decode_jwt means verify_token calls decode_jwt, emphatically not the reverse. Flip the arrow and you have flipped the question — "what do I depend on?" becomes "who depends on me?", and only one of those two prevents an outage.
Typed: the edge says calls. An untyped line between two boxes is decoration; a typed, directed edge is a machine-readable sentence you can read aloud. Twenty-two of them come out of orderflow.
steps.youDo: In graph.json, find the edge whose source is function:shared.auth.verify_token. Read it aloud as a sentence.

steps.title: Provenance — which of these twenty-two are facts
narrative: That fourth field is the one the whole course turns on. Not every edge is equally certain, and an extractor that hides the difference is a confident guesser.

This extractor grades itself with one rule you can read in forty lines of source: a call whose target resolves to a definition in the same module is a parse-tree fact — EXTRACTED. A call resolved by matching a bare name against the one definition that happens to exist elsewhere in the repo is a heuristic — INFERRED. Two or more candidates and it must emit them all as AMBIGUOUS rather than pick a favourite.

On orderflow the split is nine to thirteen. Every one of the thirteen guesses happens to be right — but "happens to be" is doing load-bearing work in that sentence, and the tag is what lets you say it out loud.
steps.youDo: Count the EXTRACTED edges yourself: grep -c EXTRACTED graph.json. At this size you can audit all nine by hand — do it.
steps.claudeSays: An agent reads the tag as a confidence floor: act on EXTRACTED, verify INFERRED before anything destructive, treat AMBIGUOUS as a question rather than an answer.

before.title: BEFORE — the rule, with a real example of each

cells: target defined in the same module — a parse-tree fact
exactly one definition of that bare name repo-wide — a guess
two or more candidates — emit all, confirm none
none here: no name in orderflow is defined twice

after.title: AFTER — the audit finding nobody advertises

cells: correct, but the count is call sites, not relationships
so 22 edges describe fewer than 22 distinct pairs
the extractor emits one edge per call site
know this before you quote an edge count at anyone

steps.title: The question a listing cannot answer
narrative: Now cash it in. Ask the question that prevents outages: if I change decode_jwt's claims format, what could break?

Invert the edge index once, then walk incoming calls edges breadth-first. Two hops later the answer includes post_invoice — a billing route that never mentions JWTs, in a different service, in a different folder. No file listing produces that, and no grep does either: the connecting facts live in two files that never share a line.

The last line is the one to sit with. Demand proof — walk EXTRACTED edges only — and the radius shrinks to one. The gap between the two numbers is your uncertainty, and it is only visible because every edge carried a tag.
steps.youDo: cd labs/M01-graph-fundamentals/solution && python graph_basics.py --check. Then change the confidence floor and watch the radius move.

terminal.text: [PASS] EXTRACTED-only radius is smaller or equal

cells: 5 hits, 3 of them prose — no def/call/mention distinction
one hop done, whole file in context

steps.title: And the size of the repo you just did this on
narrative: Thirty-six nodes. Fourteen modules. Small enough that you could have answered every question in this walkthrough by reading the code — and on a repo this size, reading the code is genuinely the cheaper move.

That is not a flaw in the exercise; it is the exercise. orderflow is a teaching graph, deliberately below the roughly 500-file line where graph tooling starts paying for itself. You built the primitives here so you can audit them; you will meet the honest cost curve in M04 and the measured four-arm benchmark in Capstone 2.

Carry forward the seven primitives, not a multiple. Nodes, typed directed edges, traversal, multi-hop paths, communities, centrality, provenance — every tool in the next eleven modules is these seven plus better extraction, storage and serving.
